facts.text: Floodwood proudly calls itself the Catfish Capital of the World, a nickname earned after launching its annual Catfish Days festival.
In 1889, plans announced a railroad would pass through Floodwood, sparking a boom that would later bring logging railroads and river transport.
Floodwood’s economy shifted to dairy in 1911 when the Floodwood Creamery Cooperative opened, supplying milk worldwide until its late‑1960s closure.
The city sits at the junction where the Floodwood, East Savanna, and Saint Louis rivers meet, a spot once vital for fur traders.
Floodwood’s first school, a log‑built structure erected in 1893, marked the town’s first organized local government the following year.
